verdict.rationale: Hyperbrowser has a first-party pricing page that tracks usage in credits bought by subscription or direct purchase. A community member who checked the pricing reported concurrency allowances, which suggests limits are published alongside plans. Another user called the credit pricing confusing and could not map it to per-page cost, and the pack never shows an explicit per-task or per-browser-hour rate or documented rate limits. Missing for 10: explicit per-task/per-browser-hour credit conversion in docs, documented API rate limits and concurrency caps per plan, independent confirmation that pricing is easy to understand.

support.subject: As a developer, I can see transparent per-task or per-browser-hour pricing and documented rate/concurrency limits before committing

citations.quote: Hyperbrowser tracks your usage via `credits` which can be acquired through a subscription or through a direct purchase.
Just did a pricing check, and you give twice as much concurrency/browsing/data-transfer as Browserbase.
